tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis:
The recorded session logs into Magento Admin, navigates to Sales > Orders grid, closes the incoming message overlay, and systematically exercises the Orders grid filters and controls: order number search, purchase date From/To, status dropdown, grand total (base and purchased) ranges, per-page selector, Search and Reset Filter buttons, pagination controls, and a View link to an individual order. It also reveals that earlier tools failed because they waited for or tried to click a non-existent selector ('a.notice-close, a[onclick*="closeMessage"]'). The new session shows the grid works fine without relying on that brittle selector; the overlay was closed via a generic indexed link, but that close step is not essential for core functionality and can be omitted.

2) Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, given filter parameters (order increment ID, purchase date range, store view, billing/shipping names, base and purchased grand total ranges, order status, page size, and page number), will: (a) ensure we are on the Sales > Orders grid (logging in if necessary), (b) apply the specified filters using robust form-field-based selectors, (c) set the desired page size and page index via pagination controls, (d) submit the Search, and (e) extract the resulting order rows and their direct View URLs. The tool must avoid the failing notice-close selector and rely on stable name- and id-based selectors or safe agentic actions only where unavoidable.

3) Action Plan:
- Step A: Navigate directly to the Sales Orders grid URL.
- Step B: If a login form is present, fill username and password and submit using stable selectors (#username, #login, and submit button by type) to reach the admin panel.
- Step C: Navigate again to the Sales Orders grid URL to land on the grid after login (Magento often redirects to dashboard first).
- Step D: Populate filters on the grid using deterministic input/select elements located by their name attributes (increment_id, created_at[from/to], store_id, billing_name, shipping_name, base_grand_total[from/to], grand_total[from/to], status). Only fill fields when corresponding inputs are non-empty parameters; otherwise leave them blank (implemented by passing empty strings).
- Step E: Set the page size (limit) using the per-page selector (select[name='limit']) if a value is provided.
- Step F: Click the Search button in the grid toolbar using a robust selector (button or span with text 'Search'), not brittle index-based selectors.
- Step G: Use pagination if a specific page is requested: click the Next or Previous pagination links the required number of times, or more robustly, use the page input/select field if available. Because the DOM from the run shows textual links 'Go to Previous page' and 'Go to Next page' rather than a numeric page input, we will implement pagination via agentic steps to click the correct pagination control based on the requested page_number relative to current page.
- Step H: Extract the order grid: for each visible row, capture order number, purchased store, purchased on date, bill-to and ship-to names, base and purchased totals, status, and the View link URL.

4) Variable Identification:
From the DOM and JSON descriptions, we can tie tool inputs to concrete field names:
- increment_id -> Order # text input: input[name='increment_id']
- created_at[from] and created_at[to] -> Purchased On date range: input[name='created_at[from]'], input[name='created_at[to]']
- store_id -> Purchased From (Store) select: select[name='store_id']
- billing_name -> Bill to Name filter: input[name='billing_name']
- shipping_name -> Ship to Name filter: input[name='shipping_name']
- base_grand_total[from] / base_grand_total[to] -> G.T. (Base) range: input[name='base_grand_total[from]'], input[name='base_grand_total[to]']
- grand_total[from] / grand_total[to] -> G.T. (Purchased) range: input[name='grand_total[from]'], input[name='grand_total[to]']
- status -> Status dropdown: select[name='status'] with known enum options like 'canceled', 'complete', etc.
- limit -> per-page selector: select[name='limit'] with allowed values 20,30,50,100,200.
- page_number -> requested page index (1-based) to navigate via pagination controls.

Authentication variables are static for this environment (admin / password123), so they are not exposed as tool inputs. All filter variables besides page_number and limit are optional; Magento accepts partially filled filters.

5) Step Optimization & Failure Fixes:
- We remove any explicit step that waits for or clicks a notice-close element such as 'a.notice-close' or 'a[onclick*="closeMessage"]' since prior attempts failed and the overlay is not essential for grid operation. If an overlay appears, it typically does not block filter row inputs; and if it did, an agentic step could dismiss it via text-based identification rather than brittle CSS selectors.
- We use direct URL navigation to the Sales Order grid instead of intermediate dashboard navigation to minimize steps.
- We use deterministic interactions by targeting form elements via their 'name' attributes, which are stable across sessions, rather than numeric highlight indexes that may change.
- We do not try to drive the store filter via the previous index-based select (which had intermittent failures); instead we use select[name='store_id'], which is semantically tied to the store filter.
- Pagination is kept simple and robust using an agentic step, because the page control structure (links vs inputs) is more dynamic and not easily represented via element hashes.
- Extraction is done in a single extract_page_content step, with a clear goal to parse and return row-level structured data and View URLs.

Because most operations are simple form interactions and a single extraction, the tool remains deterministic except for the pagination agent step, which is necessary given the dynamic nature of pagination elements.

The previous tool failure around 'a.notice-close' is explicitly addressed by not referencing that selector at all and instead relying on core grid controls only.

Given that login credentials and target URL are fixed in this environment, the input schema focuses solely on filter and pagination parameters.
name: tool_search_orders.v5
description: Locate Magento admin sales orders using flexible filters (order number, purchase date range, store view, billing/shipping names, grand total ranges, and status), control page size and pagination, and return order grid rows including direct View links. Uses robust selectors and avoids brittle notice-close selectors that failed previously.

steps.description: Open Magento Admin Sales Orders grid (may redirect to login or dashboard).
Enter Magento admin username 'admin' into the login username field if login is shown (safe even if already logged in; field will be absent in that case).
Enter Magento admin password into the login password field if login is shown.
Submit login form by clicking the 'Log in' button if present.
Ensure we are on the Sales Orders grid after login by navigating directly to the grid URL again.
Set Order # filter (increment_id). Leave empty string if no increment_id specified.
Set Purchased On From date filter (created_at[from]) in MM/DD/YYYY or leave empty.
Set Purchased On To date filter (created_at[to]) in MM/DD/YYYY or leave empty.
Set Bill to Name filter (billing_name) or leave empty.
Set Ship to Name filter (shipping_name) or leave empty.
Set Grand Total (Base) minimum filter (base_grand_total[from]) or leave empty.
Set Grand Total (Base) maximum filter (base_grand_total[to]) or leave empty.
Set Grand Total (Purchased) minimum filter (grand_total[from]) or leave empty.
Set Grand Total (Purchased) maximum filter (grand_total[to]) or leave empty.
Select Store View filter value via select[name='store_id'] when store_id is provided; otherwise this will leave the default selection.
Select Status filter value via select[name='status'] when status is provided; otherwise leave empty/any.
Set per-page row limit using select[name='limit'] when limit is provided.
Click the Search button in the Orders grid toolbar to apply all filters.
If a specific page_number is provided and greater than 1, navigate pagination links (Next/Previous or specific page controls) until that page is shown. Skip if page_number is 1 or not provided.
steps.task: If {{page_number}} is provided and greater than 1, on the Magento Sales Orders grid, use the pagination controls (e.g., links with titles or text 'Next page', 'Previous page', or numeric page inputs/selects) to navigate to page {{page_number}} of the current filtered result set. Do not change filters or page size; only adjust the current result page. Stop once the requested page number is displayed near the pagination controls.

steps.description: Extract all visible order rows and their details from the grid after filters and pagination are applied.
steps.goal: From the Magento Admin Sales Orders grid, extract for each visible row: order number, purchased store text, purchased on datetime, bill-to name, ship-to name, G.T. (Base), G.T. (Purchased), status text, and the href of the 'View' link in the Action column. Return data as a JSON array under key 'orders', and also include pagination info (current page, total pages, total records text).

input_schema.name: increment_id
input_schema.description: Order number / increment ID to search for. Maps to input[name='increment_id'].

input_schema.name: created_at_from
input_schema.description: Purchase date range start (From). Maps to input[name='created_at[from]'].

input_schema.name: created_at_to
input_schema.description: Purchase date range end (To). Maps to input[name='created_at[to]'].

input_schema.name: store_id
input_schema.description: Store View filter value for select[name='store_id'] (e.g., specific store ID as string).

input_schema.name: billing_name
input_schema.description: Billing customer name filter. Maps to input[name='billing_name'].

input_schema.name: shipping_name
input_schema.description: Shipping customer name filter. Maps to input[name='shipping_name'].

input_schema.name: base_grand_total_from
input_schema.description: Minimum base grand total filter. Maps to input[name='base_grand_total[from]'].

input_schema.name: base_grand_total_to
input_schema.description: Maximum base grand total filter. Maps to input[name='base_grand_total[to]'].

input_schema.name: grand_total_from
input_schema.description: Minimum purchased grand total filter. Maps to input[name='grand_total[from]'].

input_schema.name: grand_total_to
input_schema.description: Maximum purchased grand total filter. Maps to input[name='grand_total[to]'].

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Order status code for select[name='status']. Use empty string or omit for any status.

input_schema.name: limit
input_schema.description: Number of rows per page. Maps to select[name='limit'].

input_schema.name: page_number
input_schema.description: 1-based page number to navigate to using pagination controls after filtering.
